profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a global asset-management firm between the macro research team and the client strategy team. They are preparing a joint package for relationship managers after an internal note on the 'Maximizing Output Growth Inflation Rate' (MOGIR) in monetary policy was circulated. The immediate context is that a central-bank decision is due next week, and both teams want a consistent house view for client conversations. The agenda is to align on what goes into the shared briefing pack, who owns which artifacts, what version of the policy note will be referenced, and what 'ready for distribution' means by the end of Thursday. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the briefing structure, handoff timing, and publication workflow for the internal deck, talking points, and adviser summary.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Central-bank policy analysis, inflation dynamics, and translating academic frameworks into house research views
members.background: Elena leads the firm's macro research workstream and previously worked as an economist at a sell-side research desk; she is used to circulating concise internal notes that are later repurposed by downstream teams.
members.private_state: She wants the firm's interpretation of MOGIR to stay analytically precise and not be diluted into a simplistic 'higher inflation is good for growth' message; she is also trying to avoid spending Friday re-reviewing client-facing formatting details.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'briefing pack,' they mean the internal research deck plus the economist-approved key-message page, not the full client-distribution bundle.
The 'latest note' on MOGIR is the revised Wednesday 7:30 a.m. version in the research folder, because everyone working off the note would naturally use the newest timestamped draft.

If a package is said to be 'ready for distribution,' it means the analytical content is signed off by research and can move into client strategy's publication process, even if compliance language and adviser phrasing are still pending.
Owning the 'chart appendix' includes providing the numbers and chart titles, while downstream formatting into client templates is obviously someone else's step.

members.name: Marcus Hale
members.expertise: Turning investment research into adviser-facing narratives, distribution workflows, and cross-channel publication planning
members.background: Marcus came from a private-bank communications team and now coordinates how house views are packaged for relationship managers, email briefs, and client-call talking points.
members.private_state: He wants a usable adviser-ready package by Thursday so relationship managers can rehearse before the central-bank meeting; he is also concerned that nuanced economic language will confuse front-office teams unless it is simplified and fully templated.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'briefing pack,' they mean the complete adviser kit: deck in house template, speaker notes, one-page summary, and approved distribution copy.
The 'latest note' is the version attached in Monday's steering email, because that is the last document formally shared across teams and therefore the operative reference point.
If something is 'ready for distribution,' it means all required review steps, formatting, disclaimers, and adviser phrasing are complete enough to send directly to relationship managers.
If research owns the 'chart appendix,' they will deliver slides already formatted in the standard client deck so communications can drop them in without rebuilding.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the briefing pack
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the briefing pack' as the shared deliverable for Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the research-side package: the internal deck, core thesis on why strict inflation targeting around MOGIR supports output growth, and a short key-message page for internal reuse.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the full adviser-facing bundle: house-template slides, speaker notes, one-pager, and distribution copy that relationship managers can use immediately.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-functional firms, 'briefing pack' is a routine umbrella term, so each person hears a familiar shorthand from their own workflow and sees no reason to unpack its boundaries.

misalignment_points.topic: Which version is the latest note
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention using 'the latest note' or 'the note that went around' as the basis for materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is referring to the Wednesday revised draft in the research folder that tightens the distinction between maximizing actual output growth and simply tolerating inflation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus is referring to the Monday email attachment that was formally circulated to stakeholder teams and already informed his draft messaging grid.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents are recent, both are legitimately called the note, and because each participant is embedded in a different distribution channel, the phrase 'latest' feels self-evident rather than ambiguous.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the package should be 'ready for distribution' by end of day Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena thinks this means the economics are finalized and approved by research, after which communications and compliance can finish packaging.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus thinks this means the material is fully packaged, language-smoothed, disclaimer-complete, and sendable to relationship managers without further substantive work.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadline language in coordination meetings often compresses multiple downstream stages into one phrase, and both participants are accustomed to using 'ready' as the obvious endpoint within their own workstream.

misalignment_points.topic: How research will deliver the chart appendix
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that research will 'send over the chart appendix' for inclusion in the pack.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena plans to provide chart exports, source lines, and short analytical captions from the research deck, expecting communications to place them into the client template.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus expects research to provide already templated slides with finalized titles and visual hierarchy suitable for immediate insertion into the adviser deck.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'send over the chart appendix' sounds operationally trivial, and both sides have seen similar handoffs before, but each silently assumes the standard procedure from their own team's production system.

turns.inner_thought: I need to pin down the research-side briefing pack for this central-bank decision and make sure nobody turns MOGIR into a sloppy 'inflation helps growth' talking point. If we align the internal deck and the economist-approved message page now, downstream teams can do their part without dragging me into formatting cleanup on Friday.

turns.utterance: That makes sense. From my side, advisers really need the briefing pack by Thursday so they can prep for client conversations ahead of next week, and ideally we're ready for distribution by end of day.
